plan: Baseline: tests (11) and acceptance (9) all pass.
Contracts: low_stock consumes Inventory.items(); tested end to end, including no mutation and the strict threshold at 0 and negative values.
Integration: add, remove to 0, then report, covered in qa/test_qa_inventory.py.
Acceptance: all 8 ACs are met by the acceptance tests, so I did not duplicate them.

Edge cases: bad qty types, None, huge ints, tab/newline whitespace, validation before state change, the error type of InsufficientStock, copy semantics in both directions, and quantity() not creating entries.
Regression: discarded, because the existing code is only the version file.
Non-functional: discarded, because the architecture has no such requirement and the library is in-memory with no I/O.
test_d1_non_str_sku_raises_valueerror stays red on purpose (low severity). Rerun with: python3 -m unittest discover -s qa

defects.repro: Inventory().add(None, 1), or add(5, 1), raises AttributeError ('NoneType' object has no attribute 'strip') instead of ValueError.
defects.fix: In _normalise, raise ValueError if not isinstance(sku, str) before calling strip.
defects.if_skipped: Callers who catch ValueError for invalid arguments get an unexpected AttributeError when they pass a non-string SKU. Impact is minimal, and the signature says str.

gaps: Concurrency is out of scope per section 2, so it was not tested.
The architecture does not say how Unicode case-folding should behave (for example 'ß'.upper() is 'SS', so 'ß' and 'ss' map to the same SKU), so it was not tested.
